summary: Paginated commands must declare the response cursor path (next_max_id/cursor/continuationToken/after/has_more) the spec examples document, cursor-capable feed commands must ship --all, the lone required flag on the two highest-traffic Instagram commands doubles as a positional, numbered Instagram commands carry speaking aliases, local-store errors name a sync invocation that can actually produce the data, and 403 hints point at upstream content blocks before credentials.
reason: The generator emitted empty nextCursorPath/hasMoreField on every paginated call, so --all always stopped at page 1 while the cursors sat in the responses — dogfood sessions hand-rolled 9 cursor while-loops and lost 4 of them to shell timeouts. The same sessions hit 'required flag not set' on natural positional invocations, 'run sync first' hints for resources the default sync never covers, and a 403 hint that sent a valid API key to credential debugging when the upstream platform was blocking the content.
validated_outcome: go build/vet/test pass; new tests prove cursor-following --all merges pages and stops without a declared cursor; verify_skill.py passes; cursor paths are sourced from the archived spec's 200-response examples, so a regen can re-derive them the same way.

deferred_to_upstream.feature: Generator should derive nextCursorPath/hasMoreField from spec response examples (or live probes) when wiring paginated commands, instead of emitting empty cursor declarations that make --all a no-op.
deferred_to_upstream.reason: The cursor fields were present in the archived spec's response examples all along; this patch hand-applies per-endpoint what the generator could infer for every printed CLI. Upstream already fixed the emission path (issue #3436, closed) — a reprint under a current press supersedes the cursor-wiring half of this patch.
